source_quote: It is not a Wikipedia policy or guideline; rather, its purpose is to explain certain aspects of Wikipedia's norms or practices
statement_orig: This page is an information page, not a policy or guideline; it explains aspects of Wikipedia's norms or practices and may reflect varying levels of consensus.
statement_en: This page is an information page, not a policy or guideline; it explains aspects of Wikipedia's norms or practices and may reflect varying levels of consensus.

source_quote: A request for comment (RfC) is a way to ask the Wikipedia community for input on an issue
statement_orig: A request for comment (RfC) is a mechanism for asking the Wikipedia community for input on an issue.
statement_en: A request for comment (RfC) is a mechanism for asking the Wikipedia community for input on an issue.

source_quote: they may relate to article content pages, editorial disputes; changes to policies, guidelines, or procedures; or other topics
statement_orig: RfCs may address article content, editorial disputes, changes to policies/guidelines/procedures, or other topics.
statement_en: RfCs may address article content, editorial disputes, changes to policies/guidelines/procedures, or other topics.

source_quote: the results of a broadly-attended RfC are therefore the opposite of WP:LOCALCONSENSUS
statement_orig: A broadly-attended RfC produces community consensus, which is the opposite of local consensus.
statement_en: A broadly-attended RfC produces community consensus, which is the opposite of local consensus.

source_quote: an RfC can act as a dispute resolution
statement_orig: Because Wikipedia decides by consensus, an RfC can serve as a form of dispute resolution.
statement_en: Because Wikipedia decides by consensus, an RfC can serve as a form of dispute resolution.

source_quote: Comments are provided and discussed via an ordinary Wikipedia discussion that follows the normal talk page guidelines and procedures
statement_orig: RfC comments are provided and discussed as an ordinary talk-page discussion following normal talk page guidelines and procedures.
statement_en: RfC comments are provided and discussed as an ordinary talk-page discussion following normal talk page guidelines and procedures.

source_quote: Because consensus can change, no consensus is permanently binding, including a consensus formed in a discussion advertised via RfC
statement_orig: No consensus is permanently binding, including one formed via an RfC, because consensus can change.
statement_en: No consensus is permanently binding, including one formed via an RfC, because consensus can change.

source_quote: "RFCBEFORE" is good advice, but it's not required
statement_orig: Following RFCBEFORE (trying alternatives before an RfC) is recommended advice but is not required.
statement_en: Following RFCBEFORE (trying alternatives before an RfC) is recommended advice but is not required.

source_quote: you should try first to resolve your issues other ways
statement_orig: Before considering an RfC to resolve an editor dispute, you should first try to resolve the issue by other means.
statement_en: Before considering an RfC to resolve an editor dispute, you should first try to resolve the issue by other means.

source_quote: If you can reach a consensus or have your questions answered through discussion, then there is no need to start an RfC
statement_orig: An RfC is unnecessary if consensus can be reached or questions answered through ordinary discussion.
statement_en: An RfC is unnecessary if consensus can be reached or questions answered through ordinary discussion.

source_quote: For reporting usernames that violate the username policy, see Wikipedia:Requests for comment/User names
statement_orig: Username-policy violations should be reported at the username venue, not via the general RfC process.
statement_en: Username-policy violations should be reported at the username venue, not via the general RfC process.

source_quote: The use of requests for comment on user conduct has been discontinued
statement_orig: The RfC process must not be used for user-conduct disputes; RfC/User conduct has been discontinued.
statement_en: The RfC process must not be used for user-conduct disputes; RfC/User conduct has been discontinued.

source_quote: In severe cases of misconduct, you may try Wikipedia:Administrators' noticeboard/Incidents
statement_orig: For severe misconduct you may use the Administrators' noticeboard/Incidents, and arbitration as a last resort.
statement_en: For severe misconduct you may use the Administrators' noticeboard/Incidents, and arbitration as a last resort.

source_quote: including in that discussion an {{rfc}} template tag
statement_orig: You create an RfC by starting a talk-page/noticeboard discussion and including an {{rfc}} template tag in it.
statement_en: You create an RfC by starting a talk-page/noticeboard discussion and including an {{rfc}} template tag in it.

source_quote: That tag must be followed by a neutral and brief statement and a valid timestamp
statement_orig: The {{rfc}} tag must be followed by a neutral and brief statement and a valid timestamp.
statement_en: The {{rfc}} tag must be followed by a neutral and brief statement and a valid timestamp.

source_quote: Before starting the process, make sure that any relevant alternatives to starting an RfC have been tried
statement_orig: Before starting an RfC, you must ensure relevant alternatives have been tried.
statement_en: Before starting an RfC, you must ensure relevant alternatives have been tried.

source_quote: Open a new section at the bottom of the talk page of the article or project page that you are interested in
statement_orig: Open a new section at the bottom of the relevant article or project talk page.
statement_en: Open a new section at the bottom of the relevant article or project talk page.

source_quote: you may instead place an RfC discussion on a subpage of an appropriate, relevant page
statement_orig: When very high comment volume is expected or no relevant talk page exists, you may place the RfC on a subpage of a relevant page instead.
statement_en: When very high comment volume is expected or no relevant talk page exists, you may place the RfC on a subpage of a relevant page instead.

source_quote: The section heading should begin with "RfC" or "Request for comment"
statement_orig: The RfC section heading should begin with "RfC" or "Request for comment".
statement_en: The RfC section heading should begin with "RfC" or "Request for comment".

source_quote: Insert one {{rfc}} template tag at the top of the new talk page section, directly below the section header
statement_orig: Insert one {{rfc}} template tag at the top of the new section, directly below the header.
statement_en: Insert one {{rfc}} template tag at the top of the new section, directly below the header.

source_quote: The tag must include as parameters one or more categories from the table of RfC topics, and the category must be in lower case
statement_orig: The {{rfc}} tag must include one or more topic categories as parameters, in lower case.
statement_en: The {{rfc}} tag must include one or more topic categories as parameters, in lower case.

source_quote: If no category seems to fit, pick the one that seems closest
statement_orig: If no category fits, pick the closest one.
statement_en: If no category fits, pick the closest one.

source_quote: If the RfC is relevant to two categories, include them both in the same {{rfc}} tag
statement_orig: If two categories are relevant, include both in the same {{rfc}} tag.
statement_en: If two categories are relevant, include both in the same {{rfc}} tag.

source_quote: The "Language and linguistics" category is for requests related to a Wikipedia article ... about language and linguistics, not for requests concerning the language on a page
statement_orig: The Language and linguistics category is for articles about language/linguistics, not for questions about wording on a page.
statement_en: The Language and linguistics category is for articles about language/linguistics, not for questions about wording on a page.

source_quote: The "Wikipedia policies and guidelines" category is for discussing changes to the policies and guidelines themselves, not for discussing how to apply them to a specific case
statement_orig: The policies-and-guidelines category is for changes to policies/guidelines themselves, not for applying them to a specific case; the same applies to other non-article categories.
statement_en: The policies-and-guidelines category is for changes to policies/guidelines themselves, not for applying them to a specific case; the same applies to other non-article categories.

source_quote: Include an initial brief, neutral statement or question about the issue in the talk page section, immediately below the {{rfc}} tag
statement_orig: Include a brief, neutral initial statement or question immediately below the {{rfc}} tag.
statement_en: Include a brief, neutral initial statement or question immediately below the {{rfc}} tag.

source_quote: The statement should be self-contained, and should not assume that the section title is available
statement_orig: The initial statement should be self-contained and must not rely on the section title, which is not copied to RfC list pages.
statement_en: The initial statement should be self-contained and must not rely on the section title, which is not copied to RfC list pages.

source_quote: A long statement (including wiki markup), may be truncated or may fail to be copied at all
statement_orig: A long initial statement may be truncated or fail to copy; publish the brief neutral statement first, then add further comments below the timestamp.
statement_en: A long initial statement may be truncated or fail to copy; publish the brief neutral statement first, then add further comments below the timestamp.

source_quote: initial statements are not allowed to contain tables or complex formatting
statement_orig: Initial RfC statements must not contain tables or complex formatting.
statement_en: Initial RfC statements must not contain tables or complex formatting.

source_quote: the statement should not begin with a list
statement_orig: The initial statement should not begin with a list; if unavoidable, use   markup before the list.
statement_en: The initial statement should not begin with a list; if unavoidable, use   markup before the list.

source_quote: Add a timestamp at the end of the brief statement, using either ~~~~ ... or ~~~~~
statement_orig: Add a timestamp at the end of the statement using four tildes (~~~~) or five tildes (~~~~~); signing your username is optional.
statement_en: Add a timestamp at the end of the statement using four tildes (~~~~) or five tildes (~~~~~); signing your username is optional.

source_quote: Failing to provide a time and date will cause Legobot to remove your discussion from the pages that notify interested editors of RfCs
statement_orig: If no time and date is provided, Legobot will remove the discussion from the RfC notification pages.
statement_en: If no time and date is provided, Legobot will remove the discussion from the RfC notification pages.

source_quote: Publish the talk page edit
statement_orig: Publish the talk page edit.
statement_en: Publish the talk page edit.

source_quote: Legobot will ... advertise the RfC by copying the markup of the initial statement to a subpage of Wikipedia:Requests for comment
statement_orig: As a result of the {{rfc}} tag, Legobot advertises the RfC by copying the initial statement to an RfC listing subpage; listing may take up to a day.
statement_en: As a result of the {{rfc}} tag, Legobot advertises the RfC by copying the initial statement to an RfC listing subpage; listing may take up to a day.

source_quote: If you add another RfC category, this must not be placed after the |rfcid= parameter
statement_orig: An added RfC category must not be placed after the |rfcid= parameter, or Legobot will not process it properly.
statement_en: An added RfC category must not be placed after the |rfcid= parameter, or Legobot will not process it properly.

source_quote: You can ask for help with writing your RfC question on this page's talk page
statement_orig: You may ask for help writing your RfC question on the project talk page.
statement_en: You may ask for help writing your RfC question on the project talk page.

source_quote: The initial RfC statement (and heading) should be neutrally worded and brief
statement_orig: The initial RfC statement and heading should be neutrally worded and brief.
statement_en: The initial RfC statement and heading should be neutrally worded and brief.

source_quote: There is no actual rule saying that editors who start RfCs must make their initial explanations look like they are responses to the question
statement_orig: There is no rule requiring RfC starters to make their explanations less prominent (e.g. in a Discussion subsection).
statement_en: There is no rule requiring RfC starters to make their explanations less prominent (e.g. in a Discussion subsection).

source_quote: you may either ask someone else to write the initial statement or question, or simply do your best and leave a note asking others to improve it
statement_orig: If you cannot describe the issue neutrally, you may ask someone else to write the statement or do your best and ask others to improve it.
statement_en: If you cannot describe the issue neutrally, you may ask someone else to write the statement or do your best and ask others to improve it.

source_quote: A signature ("~~~~") or at least a time and date ("~~~~~") is required
statement_orig: A signature or at least a time and date is required in the RfC statement.
statement_en: A signature or at least a time and date is required in the RfC statement.

source_quote: Do not include any opening html tags (e.g., <small>) in the initial RfC statement unless its corresponding closing tag ... also comes before the first timestamp
statement_orig: Do not straddle the first timestamp with HTML tags; any opening tag must have its closing tag before the first timestamp.
statement_en: Do not straddle the first timestamp with HTML tags; any opening tag must have its closing tag before the first timestamp.

source_quote: the timestamp must not be placed inside a template parameter
statement_orig: The timestamp must not be placed inside a template parameter.
statement_en: The timestamp must not be placed inside a template parameter.

source_quote: It is rare for a single article, or a single editor, to have more than one or two productive RfCs open at a time
statement_orig: It is rarely productive for a single article or editor to have more than one or two RfCs open at once; check the RfC talk page before starting many.
statement_en: It is rarely productive for a single article or editor to have more than one or two RfCs open at once; check the RfC talk page before starting many.

source_quote: There is no technical limit to the number of simultaneous RfCs ... but to avoid discussion forks, they should not overlap significantly in their subject matter
statement_orig: Simultaneous RfCs on one page are technically unlimited but should not significantly overlap in subject matter, to avoid discussion forks.
statement_en: Simultaneous RfCs on one page are technically unlimited but should not significantly overlap in subject matter, to avoid discussion forks.

source_quote: Each {{rfc}} tag should also be added in a separate edit, with a delay between each edit to let the bot assign an id number
statement_orig: Each additional {{rfc}} tag should be added in a separate edit with a delay, so the bot can assign an id to the previous one first.
statement_en: Each additional {{rfc}} tag should be added in a separate edit with a delay, so the bot can assign an id to the previous one first.

source_quote: first ensure that all of the existing {{rfc}} tags already contain a |rfcid= parameter
statement_orig: Before adding a new {{rfc}} tag to a page with existing RfCs, ensure all existing tags already have a |rfcid= parameter.
statement_en: Before adding a new {{rfc}} tag to a page with existing RfCs, ensure all existing tags already have a |rfcid= parameter.

source_quote: If there are two {{rfc}} tags on the same page that both lack the |rfcid= parameter, Legobot will assign the same id number to both
statement_orig: Two {{rfc}} tags lacking |rfcid= on one page cause Legobot to assign both the same id, publicising only one; fix by removing |rfcid= from the unpublicised one and waiting.
statement_en: Two {{rfc}} tags lacking |rfcid= on one page cause Legobot to assign both the same id, publicising only one; fix by removing |rfcid= from the unpublicised one and waiting.

source_quote: you may also publicize the RfC by posting a notice at one or more of the following locations
statement_orig: You may publicize an RfC by posting a notice at relevant Village Pump forums, noticeboards, WikiProject talk pages, or related article/policy talk pages.
statement_en: You may publicize an RfC by posting a notice at relevant Village Pump forums, noticeboards, WikiProject talk pages, or related article/policy talk pages.

source_quote: When posting a notice at those locations, provide a link to the RfC, and a brief statement, but do not argue the RfC
statement_orig: When posting a publicity notice, provide a link and a brief statement but do not argue the RfC.
statement_en: When posting a publicity notice, provide a link and a brief statement but do not argue the RfC.

source_quote: Take care to adhere to the canvassing guideline, which prohibits notifying a chosen group of editors who may be biased
statement_orig: Publicity must adhere to the canvassing guideline, which prohibits notifying a chosen group of potentially biased editors.
statement_en: Publicity must adhere to the canvassing guideline, which prohibits notifying a chosen group of potentially biased editors.

source_quote: When creating a new Wikipedia policy or suggesting major modifications to a policy, follow the instructions at WP:PROPOSAL
statement_orig: When creating a new policy or proposing major policy modifications, follow the instructions at WP:PROPOSAL.
statement_en: When creating a new policy or proposing major policy modifications, follow the instructions at WP:PROPOSAL.

source_quote: Centralized discussion may be used for policy-related RfCs but is not for publicizing any content disputes in articles
statement_orig: Centralized discussion may be used for policy-related RfCs but must not be used to publicize article content disputes.
statement_en: Centralized discussion may be used for policy-related RfCs but must not be used to publicize article content disputes.

source_quote: All editors (including temporary account users) are welcome to respond to any RfC, unless there are specific behavioral restrictions in place
statement_orig: All editors, including temporary-account users, may respond to any RfC unless specific behavioral restrictions (page protection, partial blocks, ArbCom restrictions) apply.
statement_en: All editors, including temporary-account users, may respond to any RfC unless specific behavioral restrictions (page protection, partial blocks, ArbCom restrictions) apply.

source_quote: Responses may be submitted in a variety of formats
statement_orig: RfC responses may take various formats: per-editor distinct responses, threaded discussion, endorse/oppose polling on alternatives, or combinations.
statement_en: RfC responses may take various formats: per-editor distinct responses, threaded discussion, endorse/oppose polling on alternatives, or combinations.

source_quote: Editing after others have raised objections may be viewed as disruptive editing or edit warring
statement_orig: Avoid edits to content under RfC discussion that others may view as unhelpful; editing after objections may be seen as disruptive editing or edit warring.
statement_en: Avoid edits to content under RfC discussion that others may view as unhelpful; editing after objections may be seen as disruptive editing or edit warring.

source_quote: Try not to be confrontational. Be friendly and civil, and assume good faith of other editors' actions
statement_orig: When responding, be non-confrontational, friendly, civil, and assume good faith.
statement_en: When responding, be non-confrontational, friendly, civil, and assume good faith.

source_quote: identify common ground, and attempt to draw editors together rather than push them apart
statement_orig: Where possible, mediate by identifying common ground and drawing editors together.
statement_en: Where possible, mediate by identifying common ground and drawing editors together.

source_quote: Opponents of a proposal or RfC question should normally ask for help instead of boldly re-writing someone else's question
statement_orig: Opponents of an RfC question should normally ask for help rather than boldly rewriting someone else's question.
statement_en: Opponents of an RfC question should normally ask for help rather than boldly rewriting someone else's question.

source_quote: Before many editors have responded, it is acceptable to modify the question
statement_orig: Before many editors have responded, it is acceptable to modify the RfC question (e.g. if participants are confused).
statement_en: Before many editors have responded, it is acceptable to modify the RfC question (e.g. if participants are confused).

source_quote: add a very brief summary question to the top (after the {{rfc}} tag but before the first timestamp)
statement_orig: If the original question is too long or malformed, add a very brief summary question after the {{rfc}} tag but before the first timestamp.
statement_en: If the original question is too long or malformed, add a very brief summary question after the {{rfc}} tag but before the first timestamp.

source_quote: Add an alternative unbiased statement immediately below the original RfC question
statement_orig: You may add an alternative unbiased statement immediately below the original question, after the {{rfc}} tag and first timestamp.
statement_en: You may add an alternative unbiased statement immediately below the original question, after the {{rfc}} tag and first timestamp.

source_quote: Do not end an RfC just because you think the wording is biased
statement_orig: You must not end an RfC merely because you think the wording is biased.
statement_en: You must not end an RfC merely because you think the wording is biased.

source_quote: An {{rfc}} tag generally remains on the page until removed by Legobot or the originator. An RfC can be ended only when the criteria at Ending RfCs are met
statement_orig: An {{rfc}} tag remains until removed by Legobot or the originator, and an RfC may be ended only when the Ending-RfCs criteria are met.
statement_en: An {{rfc}} tag remains until removed by Legobot or the originator, and an RfC may be ended only when the Ending-RfCs criteria are met.

source_quote: Ending an RfC ... Removing the link to the discussion from the central RfC lists
statement_orig: Ending an RfC means removing the discussion link from the central RfC lists by removing the {{rfc}} tag; a bot handles the rest.
statement_en: Ending an RfC means removing the discussion link from the central RfC lists by removing the {{rfc}} tag; a bot handles the rest.

source_quote: The end of a discussion ... This means people have stopped discussing the question
statement_orig: The end of a discussion means people have stopped discussing the question; when it naturally ends you should consider ending the RfC.
statement_en: The end of a discussion means people have stopped discussing the question; when it naturally ends you should consider ending the RfC.

source_quote: Closing the discussion ... Someone lists conclusions (if any) and discourages further discussion
statement_orig: Closing a discussion means someone lists conclusions and discourages further discussion; closing and summarizing are distinct and neither is required.
statement_en: Closing a discussion means someone lists conclusions and discourages further discussion; closing and summarizing are distinct and neither is required.

source_quote: There is no required minimum or maximum duration; typically 7 days is a minimum, and after 30 days the discussion is ripe for closure
statement_orig: An RfC has no required minimum or maximum duration; typically 7 days is a minimum and after 30 days it is ripe for closure.
statement_en: An RfC has no required minimum or maximum duration; typically 7 days is a minimum and after 30 days it is ripe for closure.

source_quote: Legobot ... automatically ends it (removes the {{rfc}} tag) 30 days after it begins
statement_orig: Legobot automatically ends an RfC by removing the {{rfc}} tag 30 days after it begins.
statement_en: Legobot automatically ends an RfC by removing the {{rfc}} tag 30 days after it begins.

source_quote: editors should not wait for that. If one of the reasons to end RfCs applies, someone should end it manually
statement_orig: Editors should not wait for auto-expiry; if a reason to end applies, someone should end the RfC manually as soon as it has run its course.
statement_en: Editors should not wait for auto-expiry; if a reason to end applies, someone should end the RfC manually as soon as it has run its course.

source_quote: To extend a current RfC for another 30 days ... insert a current timestamp immediately before the original timestamp of the opening statement
statement_orig: To extend an RfC by 30 days and prevent Legobot auto-ending, insert a current timestamp immediately before the opening statement's original timestamp.
statement_en: To extend an RfC by 30 days and prevent Legobot auto-ending, insert a current timestamp immediately before the opening statement's original timestamp.

source_quote: The question may be withdrawn by the poster
statement_orig: The RfC question may be withdrawn by its poster, who would normally remove the {{rfc}} tag.
statement_en: The RfC question may be withdrawn by its poster, who would normally remove the {{rfc}} tag.

source_quote: The RfC participants can agree to end it at any time; one of them removes the {{rfc}} tag
statement_orig: RfC participants may agree to end the RfC at any time, with one of them removing the {{rfc}} tag.
statement_en: RfC participants may agree to end the RfC at any time, with one of them removing the {{rfc}} tag.

source_quote: Any uninvolved editor can post a closing summary of the discussion; if consensus is undoubtedly clear, even an involved editor may summarize
statement_orig: Any uninvolved editor may post a closing summary; an involved editor may summarize only if consensus is undoubtedly clear.
statement_en: Any uninvolved editor may post a closing summary; an involved editor may summarize only if consensus is undoubtedly clear.

source_quote: The editor removes the {{rfc}} tag while closing the discussion
statement_orig: The editor closing an RfC removes the {{rfc}} tag while closing the discussion.
statement_en: The editor closing an RfC removes the {{rfc}} tag while closing the discussion.

source_quote: involved editors (on all sides of a dispute) are encouraged to let someone else write a summary
statement_orig: To avoid biased-summary concerns, involved editors on all sides are encouraged to let someone else write the summary (WP:NACINV).
statement_en: To avoid biased-summary concerns, involved editors on all sides are encouraged to let someone else write the summary (WP:NACINV).

source_quote: Please remove the {{rfc}} tag when the dispute has been resolved, or when discussion has ended
statement_orig: Remove the {{rfc}} tag when the dispute is resolved or discussion has ended.
statement_en: Remove the {{rfc}} tag when the dispute is resolved or discussion has ended.

source_quote: To end an RfC manually, remove the {{rfc}} tag from the talk page
statement_orig: To end an RfC manually, remove the {{rfc}} tag from the talk page; Legobot removes the discussion from the central lists on its next run.
statement_en: To end an RfC manually, remove the {{rfc}} tag from the talk page; Legobot removes the discussion from the central lists on its next run.

source_quote: If you are also closing the discussion, you should do this in the same edit
statement_orig: If you are also closing the discussion when ending an RfC, do it in the same edit.
statement_en: If you are also closing the discussion when ending an RfC, do it in the same edit.

source_quote: Do not enclose the {{rfc}} tag in <nowiki>...</nowiki> or <syntaxhighlight>...</syntaxhighlight> tags, nor place it in HTML comment markers
statement_orig: Do not enclose the {{rfc}} tag in nowiki, syntaxhighlight, or HTML comment markers, since Legobot will ignore these and treat the RfC as still open.
statement_en: Do not enclose the {{rfc}} tag in nowiki, syntaxhighlight, or HTML comment markers, since Legobot will ignore these and treat the RfC as still open.

source_quote: can formally request closure by posting at Wikipedia:Closure requests
statement_orig: Anyone wanting an uninvolved editor to write a closing summary can formally request closure at Wikipedia:Closure requests.
statement_en: Anyone wanting an uninvolved editor to write a closing summary can formally request closure at Wikipedia:Closure requests.

source_quote: If the matter under discussion is not contentious and the consensus is obvious ... then formal closure is neither necessary nor advisable
statement_orig: If the matter is uncontentious and consensus is obvious to participants, formal closure is neither necessary nor advisable.
statement_en: If the matter is uncontentious and consensus is obvious to participants, formal closure is neither necessary nor advisable.

source_quote: Written closing statements are not required. Editors are expected to be able to evaluate and agree upon the results of most RfCs without outside assistance
statement_orig: Written closing statements are not required; editors are expected to evaluate and agree on most RfC results without outside assistance.
statement_en: Written closing statements are not required; editors are expected to evaluate and agree on most RfC results without outside assistance.

source_quote: you may optionally enclose the talk page section in a box using a tag pair such as {{closed rfc top}}/{{closed rfc bottom}}
statement_orig: To alert readers an RfC has ended, you may optionally box the section with a tag pair such as {{closed rfc top}}/{{closed rfc bottom}}; this is not required.
statement_en: To alert readers an RfC has ended, you may optionally box the section with a tag pair such as {{closed rfc top}}/{{closed rfc bottom}}; this is not required.

source_quote: If a closed RfC discussion results in a major policy change, strongly consider updating related guides such as Help:Introduction to Wikipedia
statement_orig: If a closed RfC results in a major policy change, strongly consider updating related guides such as Help:Introduction to Wikipedia.
statement_en: If a closed RfC results in a major policy change, strongly consider updating related guides such as Help:Introduction to Wikipedia.

source_quote: Anyone who wants to have more comments on the topic can restart an RfC that has ended, as long as the discussion has not been closed
statement_orig: Anyone may restart an ended RfC to gather more comments, provided the discussion has not been closed.
statement_en: Anyone may restart an ended RfC to gather more comments, provided the discussion has not been closed.

source_quote: To restart an RfC, reinsert the {{rfc}} tag. If it was automatically removed by Legobot, then be sure to insert a current timestamp after the RfC statement, and before its original timestamp
statement_orig: To restart an RfC, reinsert the {{rfc}} tag; if Legobot auto-removed it, insert a current timestamp after the statement and before the original timestamp, or it will be re-removed.
statement_en: To restart an RfC, reinsert the {{rfc}} tag; if Legobot auto-removed it, insert a current timestamp after the statement and before the original timestamp, or it will be re-removed.

source_quote: if the RfC is to be of long duration, you may instead add the line <!-- RFCBot Ignore Expired --> before the {{rfc}} tag
statement_orig: For a long-duration RfC, you may add <!-- RFCBot Ignore Expired --> before the {{rfc}} tag instead of repeatedly extending.
statement_en: For a long-duration RfC, you may add <!-- RFCBot Ignore Expired --> before the {{rfc}} tag instead of repeatedly extending.

source_quote: You should mention at the end of the RfC statement that the RfC ended and restarted, and add your signature if appropriate
statement_orig: When restarting, you should note at the end of the RfC statement that it ended and restarted, and sign if appropriate.
statement_en: When restarting, you should note at the end of the RfC statement that it ended and restarted, and sign if appropriate.

source_quote: Add the tag {{rfc|xxx}} at the top of a talk page section, where "xxx" is the category abbreviation
statement_orig: To add a discussion to the RfC list, add {{rfc|xxx}} at the top of a talk-page section, with xxx the category abbreviation; multiple categories are pipe-separated.
statement_en: To add a discussion to the RfC list, add {{rfc|xxx}} at the top of a talk-page section, with xxx the category abbreviation; multiple categories are pipe-separated.

source_quote: Lists are updated every hour by Legobot
statement_orig: The RfC lists are updated every hour by Legobot.
statement_en: The RfC lists are updated every hour by Legobot.
